notes: §1985:VII.4.5.2 prints the sequential REWRITE as 'REWRITE record-name-1 [FROM identifier-1] [END-REWRITE]'. CobolIO.g4#rewriteStatement parses it and SequentialIoBinder#BindRewrite binds it; at 85 the 2002+ arms are refused: FROM literal/ALL literal (COBOL0871, VisitRecordFromPhrase), WITH [NO] LOCK and RETRY (COBOL0900), FILE file-name (COBOL1706, DeclinedFilePhrase), INVALID KEY on a sequential file (COBOL1720, ScreenForbiddenPhrase), a doubled FROM or an empty REWRITE (parse errors). Probes at 85: FROM a group, a ref-modified item and FUNCTION UPPER-CASE run; REWRITE after OPEN INPUT 49, without a prior READ 43 (§1985:VII.4.5.4 GR2), a RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON size change 44 (GR10). The witness REWRITEs FROM identifier with END-REWRITE and reads NEW01 back. Lead outside this row: an FD with two 01s of 5 and 8 characters and no RECORD clause writes every record padded to 8, so REWRITE of the 5-character record gives 44; §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR1 makes that 'implementor' latitude ambiguous (2023 §13.18.43.4 GR5 implicit RECORD clause), for the GR10 row. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5159 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-10.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-10-refute.json).

next.reason: §1985:VII.4.5.2, the sequential REWRITE, is 'REWRITE record-name-1 [FROM identifier-1] [END-REWRITE]' with no INVALID KEY phrase. §2023:14.9.35.2 is one REWRITE format for every organization; it accepts the 1985 form with the same meaning, and §2023:14.9.35.3 SR2 ('Neither the INVALID KEY phrase nor the NOT INVALID KEY phrase shall be specified for a REWRITE statement that references a file with sequential organization') keeps the 1985 sequential restriction. But it adds 'FILE file-name-1', 'FROM literal-1', the retry-phrase and WITH [NO] LOCK, all refused by the 1985 format: wider, no exception condition, CHANGED.
